attributes.residual: NONE in .text. THE FINDING, and it corrects the predecessor record's prescription while confirming its diagnosis. attempt.EN_...20260904.v1 said the rule 'must be authored in the VALUE-EQUALITY mode (verify_value_equality_recolor, as do_enemies' shipped pin uses), never the plain copy_register_fields'. That is the wrong cure for the right reason. The defect at +0x1dc..+0x1e8 is NOT a recolor question in any mode: `wf_ordered_datum_screen.py` classified it as `DEFECT ... 1 DATUM-SWAP row(s): the same register, at the same position and under the same mnemonic, receives a DIFFERENT datum, and the two datums appear in each other's slot`, listing `[18] DATUM-SWAP T@lfd f30,0(0) lbl_80346840 (B:400921fb54524550) O@lfd f30,0(0) @689 (B:401921fb54524550)` -- the SAME register f30 on BOTH sides, holding pi in the target and 2*pi in ours. A rule that only rewrites register fields has no way to express that, because the register field is already correct; what is wrong is which relocation sits at that index. The value-equality mode would not have helped, and declaring it would have been the second unsound rule on this function in two runs. The permutation stage is the only stage that MOVES relocations with their atoms, and the mechanical proof that it did is that the window's `before_relocations_sha256` and `after_relocations_sha256` DIFFER. Note also that `wf_word_diff.py` reported `RELOC-SYMBOL MISMATCH = 0` for this function throughout, before and after: it cannot see the transposition, because our anonymous @688/@689 cannot be name-compared against the target's lbl_ names. The word diff is therefore NOT the screen that decides a pool-order residual; the ordered-datum screen is.

windows_tried: EXACTLY ONE window was authored and it was derived, not searched: ["0x1dc:0x1ec:2,3,0,1"]. It was chosen by reading the aligned view rather than by trying orders -- `fnasm.py game/enemy/enemy.c move_logic00 0x1d0:0x1f8 --diff` shows two INTERLEAVED transposed pairs inside one four-instruction span (the two pooled f64 constants at +0x1dc/+0x1e4 and the two counter initialisations at +0x1e0/+0x1e8), so the window has to span all four atoms and the order is forced. The narrower two-atom window ["0x1dc:0x1e8:2,1,0"] that closes only the constants was considered and rejected before any build: it leaves the two `li` rows transposed, which is precisely the inconsistency the negative control below reports at +0x204.
